method: Direct retrieval of public institutional/scholarly pages with the session fetch tool (no shell network calls). Priority: flagged statements (line 51), wrong-fit citations, and language/material or language/myth couplings rather than isolated bibliography facts. Primary-text excerpts below were taken from retrieved page text; ctext.org refused automated retrieval and its terms were respected, so Wikisource transcriptions were used for the Chinese classics (limit noted per row). Web search was quota-blocked after the first query, so discovery ran through J-STAGE's own on-site search and e-Gov's law-data endpoints.

audits.claim: The canonical five colours (五色: qing, chi red, huang yellow, bai white, hei black) are bound to directions in the Zhouli's Kaogong ji, with centre-yellow among them.
audits.entry_locator: §5 'Chinese qing 青' bullet, sentence 'Embedded in the canonical five colors (五色 …) bound to Five Phases and directions — east-qing/dragon, … center-huang (Kaogong ji in the Zhouli; Needham 1956)' (line 58)
audits.retrieval_status: retrieved: full 冬官考工記 chapter transcription (long page, complete chapter from 國有六職 to the closing 弓人 section)
audits.source_locator: 冬官考工記, '畫繢之事' passage (second half of the chapter, immediately before the 鍾氏染羽 dyeing passage)
audits.source_excerpt: 畫繢之事：雜五色。東方謂之青，南方謂之赤，西方謂之白，北方謂之黑，天謂之玄，地謂之黃。
audits.basis: PASSAGE RETRIEVED verbatim. The direction–colour pairs 東方青 / 南方赤 / 西方白 / 北方黑 match the entry's east-qing, south-chi, west-bai, north-hei exactly, and 'centre-huang' follows from 地謂之黃 (earth-yellow) in the same run — an inference the entry's wording does not spell out, so it is safe but indirect. The passage is in the 設色 (colour-laying) section of the chapter, i.e. it is a craft/ritual colour scheme, which is the entry's own framing. The retrieved chapter does not itself name the Five Phases (五行); that layer comes from the correlative literature (see COL-02).
audits.access_limit: Wikisource community transcription (base text with the transmitted commentary apparatus stripped); not collated against a print or critical edition, no variant readings checked.

audits.claim: The animal glyphs east-qing/dragon, south-chi/bird, west-bai/tiger, north-hei/tortoise-snake, centre-huang are carried by the citation '(Kaogong ji in the Zhouli; Needham 1956)'.
audits.retrieval_status: retrieved: full 淮南子·天文訓 chapter transcription
audits.source_locator: 天文訓, '何謂五星' passage (the five-phase/direction scheme: 東方木 … 北方水)
audits.source_excerpt: 其獸蒼龍，其音角，其日甲乙。南方，火也…其獸朱鳥…中央，土也…其獸黃龍…西方，金也…其獸白虎…北方，水也…其獸玄武
audits.basis: The glyph set the entry cites is NOT in the cited source and IS in a different one. In the retrieved 考工記 chapter (COL-01's source) the '畫繢之事' passage carries direction–colour pairs only — no dragon, bird, tiger or tortoise-snake. The chapter's only such emblem list is attached to flags and lodges, not to colours: '龍旗九斿，以象大火也。鳥旟七斿，以象鶉火也。熊旗六斿，以象伐也。龜蛇四斿，以象營室也' — note its western emblem is 熊 (bear), not 虎 (tiger). The exact five-fold beast set is retrieved instead in 淮南子·天文訓 (Han, 2nd c. BCE): 蒼龍 east, 朱鳥 south, 黃龍 centre, 白虎 west, 玄武 north, each inside a 五星/五行 scheme. All five fragments in source_excerpt occur verbatim in the retrieved passage (ellipses join non-adjacent fragments). Dated erratum appended to the entry correcting the citation coverage only; the claim's content is not contradicted.
audits.access_limit: Wikisource community transcription, not collated against print editions; authorship/date of 淮南子 not re-verified against a critical edition in this pass.

audits.claim: Xunzi, 'Quanxue' (c. 3rd c. BCE) carries 'blue comes from the indigo plant, yet is bluer than the plant' (青出於藍) — the dye-source word (lan 藍) and the hue word in one line.
audits.retrieval_status: retrieved: full 勸學篇 page text, including the transmitted commentary
audits.source_locator: 勸學篇, opening sentence block ('君子曰：學不可以已…')
audits.source_excerpt: 君子曰：學不可以已。靑，取之於藍而靑於藍；冰，水爲之而寒於水。
audits.basis: PASSAGE RETRIEVED verbatim (靑 is the page's glyph variant of 青). The line does place the dye plant 藍 and the colour word 靑 in the same image, which is what the entry cites it for, and 青出於藍 is indeed the 勸學篇 opening stock phrase. Limit kept explicit: the broader lexicographic step ('the dye-source word becomes the hue word') is not established by this line alone — no dictionary entry for 藍 was retrieved, so the word-history half of the bullet remains an inference from this quotation.
audits.access_limit: Wikisource transcription of a commented edition (楊倞-type commentary interleaved); no critical apparatus and no date-independent textual history checked.

audits.claim: The Xunzi passage is dated c. 3rd c. BCE.
audits.entry_locator: §5 'Plant→color path, documented' bullet (line 59), parenthetical 'Xunzi, "Quanxue" (c. 3rd c. BCE)'
audits.retrieval_status: retrieved: full encyclopedia article (Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy), HTML
audits.source_locator: title line and §1 'Life and Work', second paragraph (on the received text)
audits.source_excerpt: Xunzi (Hsün Tzu, c. 310—c. 220 B.C.E.) … the Xunzi that we have today is a later compilation of writings associated with him, not all of which were necessarily written by Xunzi himself
audits.basis: PASSAGE RETRIEVED. The dates place the philosopher inside the 3rd c. BCE (Warring States), so the entry's 'c. 3rd c. BCE' is the standard scholarly framing, and the retrieved text also supplies the caveat the entry does not carry: the received book is a later compilation. That caveat qualifies attribution of individual chapters but does not move the date, and the entry neither claims a specific year nor a holograph.
audits.access_limit: IEP is a peer-reviewed general reference work (article by D. Elstein, SUNY New Paltz), not a critical edition; no epigraphic or manuscript dating re-examined.

audits.claim: The Japanese go-light's lens shade sits at the blue end of the CIE green range after a 1973 administrative step, so the signal colour deviates from the CIE recommendation; the signal is officially called the 'blue signal'.
audits.entry_locator: §4 traffic-light bullet, sentence 'the lens shade sits at the blue end of the CIE green range since a 1973 administrative step … treat the date as reported, not settled (Atlas Obscura 2017; 照明学会誌 64(6) 1980 on the CIE 色度推奨範囲)' (line 51)
audits.retrieval_status: retrieved: J-STAGE on-site search-results page text; row-level metadata plus publisher abstracts; article landing pages/PDFs not opened
audits.source_locator: result rows '阿山 みよし, 高橋 澪子, 片寄 隆正, 高須 陽介, 照明学会誌, 1982年, 66巻10号, 445-449, フリー' and '照明学会誌, 1988年, 72巻2号, 109-114' with their English abstracts
audits.source_excerpt: The recommended color boundaries in the chromaticity diagram for the light signals of road traffic control in Japan are considerably different from the CIE recommendation especially as concerns the 'blue signal'.
audits.basis: ABSTRACT TEXT RETRIEVED from the publisher's own index, and the same 1982 abstract opens 'we have often found that the go-signal called as a "blue signal" does not appear blue, sometimes they are rather green', i.e. it independently documents both the designator and the hue deviation from CIE. This corroborates the entry's substantive point (Japanese signal chromatics is bluer than the CIE green) with a period scholarly source. It does NOT supply the 1973 date: the entry's own flag ('reported, not settled') is left standing, and the entry's cited 照明学会誌 64(6):315-318 (1980) did not appear in this result set and was not retrieved.
audits.access_limit: Abstract-level retrieval only (search-results page); 1982/1988 full texts and the cited 1980 article not obtained; no DOI-level landing page reached (J-STAGE article paths tried returned HTTP 404).

audits.claim: The go-light is 青色の灯火 in 道路交通法施行令 art. 2 (official statutory wording behind the ao-shingō collocation).
audits.entry_locator: §4 traffic-light bullet, 'traffic lights are officially ao shingō (青信号 — the go-light is 青色の灯火 in 道路交通法施行令 art. 2)' (line 51)
audits.retrieval_status: partial/blocked: law-data endpoint responded and served the ordinance text, but the extraction truncates at Article 1; the human-facing document page requires JavaScript; the legacy host law.e-gov.go.jp no longer resolves (DNS) and the v2 JSON endpoint returned HTTP 404 on the new domain
audits.source_locator: retrieved fragment covers 第一条（歩行補助車等） only; 第二条（信号の意味） not reached in the retrieved bytes
audits.source_excerpt: 道路交通法（以下「法」という。）第二条第一項第九号の歩行補助車等は、次に掲げるもの…
audits.basis: The endpoint demonstrably serves this ordinance (Article 1 text retrieved), but the retrieved bytes stop before Article 2, so the statutory phrase 青色の灯火 could not be confirmed from an institutional full text in this pass, and no substitute official text (police-agency page, Japanese Law Translation, NDL) was reached. Nothing here suggests the entry is wrong; the claim simply stays unverified, consistent with the entry's own caution on the date.
audits.access_limit: e-Gov text extraction truncated at Article 1 across both the old and the new domain; two URL forms of the v2 law_data API returned 404; no bypass attempted.

audits.claim: The catchphrase 四十八茶百鼠 is figurative ('many', not a count) and is a later label of the traditional-colour literature rather than a located Edo-period document (NDL レファレンス協同データベース no. 1000168280; 長崎盛輝 1988; 吉岡幸雄 2000).
audits.retrieval_status: blocked: HTTP 403 on both the detail and entry URL forms of the NDL Collaborative Reference Database; NDL Search API routes returned no extractable text
audits.basis: The institutional record the entry leans on could not be read by this agent, so the era/dress coupling it supports (Edo sumptuary austerity → named muted-colour vocabulary, with the phrase's numbers read as figurative) remains unverified in this pass. No substitute institutional source was retrieved and none is named here, and the entry's own hedge is left untouched. Because this is a failure to retrieve rather than a retrieved contradiction, nothing was appended to the entry.
audits.access_limit: HTTP 403 (bot-blocked); no scraping workaround attempted, by policy.

unresolved_or_blocked: 道路交通法施行令 article 2 text not obtained: e-Gov law-data extraction truncates at Article 1; document UI needs JavaScript; legacy law.e-gov.go.jp DNS-fails; laws.e-gov.go.jp v2 law_data endpoint HTTP 404 (COL-06).
NDL Collaborative Reference Database record 1000168280 HTTP 403 on two URL forms; NDL Search OpenSearch endpoints yielded no extractable text (COL-07).

照明学会誌 64(6):315-318 (1980), the entry's cited CIE-chromaticity item, was not retrieved; J-STAGE discovery is limited to the on-site result page available in this session, and J-STAGE article landing paths tried returned HTTP 404 (COL-05).

ctext.org refused automated retrieval and explicitly denies scraping authorization; Wikisource transcriptions were used instead for 考工記, 荀子 and 淮南子, with the transcription-level limit recorded on those rows (COL-01 to COL-03).

Web search was quota-blocked after one query, so no additional scholarly/institutional cross-checks were discovered beyond the sources named above; the 1973 administrative date for the signal-colour shift remains reported-only, exactly as the entry flags it.

entry_edit.summary: COL-02 correction appended 2026-10-17: the entry's §5 parenthetical attributing east-qing/dragon … north-hei/tortoise-snake to the Kaogong ji over-covers the animal glyphs; the retrieved 考工記 chapter carries direction–colour pairs only (東方謂之青…地謂之黃) and its dragon/bird/bear/tortoise-snake emblems attach to flags and astronomical lodges (west = bear, not tiger), while the five-fold beast set is retrieved in 淮南子·天文訓. Claim content retained; citation coverage corrected; no old bytes deleted.
